content: stripe webhooks keep double-charging customers when the endpoint times out

The double charge happens because Stripe retries the webhook and your handler creates a new PaymentIntent each delivery. Fix: make the handler idempotent — store event.id in a processed_events table with a unique constraint, return 200 immediately on duplicate, and move the slow fulfillment work into a queue so the endpoint responds inside Stripe's 20s window.
what about events that arrive out of order, like invoice.paid before invoice.created?

Don't trust webhook ordering at all — Stripe explicitly doesn't guarantee it. Treat every event as a trigger to re-fetch the object's current state from the API and reconcile against your database, rather than applying the event payload as a delta. That makes ordering irrelevant.
the product grid page rerenders everything when I hover one card, react devtools shows the whole tree flashing

Root cause: the hover handler sets state in the grid parent, and every ProductCard receives a new inline style object each render so React.memo never bails out. Fixes: move hover state into the card itself, wrap ProductCard in memo with a stable props shape, and hoist the style object out of render. After that only the hovered card re-renders — verified with the profiler, commit render count dropped from 240 to 2.
can we also stop the images from refetching on every rerender
The refetch was the cache-busting query param built from Date.now() in the srcset helper. Remove it and let the CDN etag handle freshness; images now come from memory cache on rerender.
docker builds in CI take 11 minutes, locally they're 90 seconds, what's wrong with the cache

CI starts from a clean daemon every run so there is no local layer cache. Enable BuildKit's registry cache: build with --cache-from type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/org/app:buildcache and --cache-to mode=max on the same ref. Also reorder the Dockerfile: COPY package.json + lockfile and run npm ci before COPY . so dependency layers survive source-only changes. CI build dropped to 2m40s.
the arm64 build is still slow on the amd64 runner

That's QEMU emulation — cross-compiling in a single-arch stage with GOARCH=arm64 (or using native arm64 runners for that matrix leg) avoids emulating the whole toolchain. QEMU is fine for the final copy stage but never for compilation.
postgres query on events table went from 40ms to 9 seconds over a month, table is 200M rows

The composite index on (account_id, created_at) is bloated: pgstattuple shows 68% dead space because the table gets high-churn updates and autovacuum can't keep up on a table this size. Short term: REINDEX CONCURRENTLY. Long term: raise autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor granularity by setting per-table storage parameters (autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor=0.01) and consider partitioning by month so vacuums stay small.
after the reindex it's 60ms but the planner still picks a seq scan for last-hour queries

Stats are stale — run ANALYZE after the reindex, and for the last-hour pattern add a partial index WHERE created_at > now() - interval '7 days' is not possible (non-immutable), so use a BRIN index on created_at instead: tiny, and perfect for append-mostly time ranges.
users get logged out randomly, jwt verification fails with invalid signature but only sometimes

Intermittent invalid-signature with multiple instances means key skew: instance A signs with the new rotated secret while instance B still verifies with the old one from its env cache. Fix: verify against a keyset, not a single secret — publish kid in the JWT header, keep both keys valid during rotation windows, and have instances refresh the JWKS every 5 minutes. The logouts were exactly correlated with your Friday secret rotations.
should refresh tokens go in localStorage or a cookie

httpOnly Secure SameSite=Lax cookie for the refresh token — localStorage is readable by any XSS payload. Keep the short-lived access token in memory only. Add CSRF protection on the refresh endpoint since cookies ride along automatically.
the checkout summary sidebar overlaps the footer on short viewports with css grid

The sidebar uses position: sticky inside a grid track whose height comes from the taller main column, and on short viewports its sticky box is taller than the viewport so it escapes into the footer visually. Fix: give the sidebar max-height: calc(100vh - var(--header-h)) with overflow-y: auto, and set align-self: start so the sticky element's containing block is the track, not the stretched cell.
pandas merge between orders and refunds silently drops 3000 rows

Your order_id columns have mismatched dtypes: orders reads as int64 but refunds comes from the CSV with NaNs so pandas promoted it to float64, and 1044859 became 1044859.0 — merge keys never match. Cast both sides explicitly with astype('Int64') (nullable integer) before merging, and add validate='one_to_many' plus an anti-join count assertion so silent drops become loud failures.
good catch, add a coverage report for the join

Added a match-coverage block after the merge: total refunds, matched, unmatched with the top 10 unmatched ids printed. It runs on every pipeline execution and fails the job if coverage drops under 99.5%.
redis cache serves stale user profiles after the profile service writes an update

You're doing cache-aside with a 15 minute TTL and no invalidation on write. Options ranked: (1) write-through — the profile service updates Redis in the same transaction boundary as Postgres, (2) delete-on-write and let the next read repopulate, (3) short TTL as a backstop. We went with delete-on-write plus a 60s TTL floor, and added a version field in the cached blob so readers can detect torn updates. Stale reads dropped to zero in the canary.
github actions matrix runs the expensive integration suite 9 times, once per combo, need it once

Split the workflow: keep the 3x3 matrix for unit tests, and pull integration into a separate job that needs: [unit] with a single runner, gated by if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'. For the matrix legs, add exclude: entries for the redundant OS/node combos nobody ships on. Total CI minutes dropped 64%.
websocket clients reconnect in a thundering herd after a deploy and knock the gateway over

All 40k clients see the close at the same instant and retry immediately. Client fix: exponential backoff with full jitter (random between 0 and min(cap, base*2^attempt)) — never equal-spaced retries. Server fix: drain connections gradually on deploy with a GOAWAY-style close spread over 60s, and have the LB reject with 503 + Retry-After when the gateway is above 80% capacity so clients back off before the socket even opens.
s3 presigned upload urls fail with SignatureDoesNotMatch only from the browser, curl works

The browser adds Content-Type to the PUT, but the URL was presigned without it, so the signature doesn't cover the header the browser sends. Presign with the exact ContentType the client will use (pass it from the file picker), or presign a POST policy which tolerates extra fields. Also your clock-skew retry: the 15 minute expiry plus the user leaving the tab open explains the second batch of failures — regenerate the URL on submit, not on page load.
sqlite database is locked errors when the background sync and the UI write at the same time

You're on the default rollback journal. Switch to WAL mode (PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL) so readers never block the writer, set busy_timeout=5000 so brief write contention waits instead of throwing, and funnel all writes through one connection per process. Keep transactions short — the sync loop held one open across a network call, which is what actually serialized everything.
terraform apply hangs on acquiring state lock and then errors, someone's lock is stuck from a killed run

A CI job was cancelled mid-apply and never released the DynamoDB lock. Confirm nobody is actually applying (check the LockID's Info field for who/when), then terraform force-unlock <lock-id>. Prevention: give CI applies a timeout lower than the job timeout, and add -lock-timeout=5m so queued runs wait politely instead of failing instantly.
npm publish from CI fails with 403 even though the token has publish rights

Three separate causes stacked: the package name was scoped and private by default (needs publish --access public the first time), provenance requires id-token: write permission in the workflow, and the granular token was pinned to the old package name from before the rename. After fixing all three the tag-triggered release worked; kept --provenance since it gives consumers a verifiable build attestation.
